paper.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools

audit_focus: Separation of paper's empirical findings from KAD deterministic/probabilistic architectural framing

investigation.primary_paper_text: Toolformer is trained to decide which APIs to call, when to call them, what arguments to pass, and how to incorporate the results... Filtering criterion: given a position i and candidate API call c_i with execution result r_i, we compute the weighted cross-entropy loss over subsequent tokens. An API call is kept if L_i(r_i) - min(L_i(empty), L_i(r_empty)) > tau_f (threshold).
investigation.diagnosis: The finding that Toolformer achieves strong zero-shot performance on downstream benchmarks by filtering API calls that reduce next-token perplexity is a SOURCE_FACT. Framing this as 'deterministic execution overcoming probabilistic limits' is a valid KAD-PI systems engineering synthesis, but was incorrectly labeled as a direct paper finding in WP-006.

remediation.source_fact_restated: Toolformer learns self-supervised API call insertion by retaining only those calls where the tool execution result strictly reduces cross-entropy loss on subsequent token prediction, improving zero-shot benchmark performance on arithmetic (ASDiv, SVAMP), QA (LAMA), and temporal reasoning (TempLAMA).
remediation.synthesis_reclassified: Interpreting API execution as a deterministic verification and grounding mechanism that bounds probabilistic language model generation is classified as DERIVED_SYNTHESIS / PROJECT_INFERENCE.
